title: the Brahmanda
tomorrow: a goddess rises from a fire holding flowers. why flowers?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Skanda, and the Satyanarayana katha: a promise put off, and a blessing not to walk past. Today, a Purana named for everything at once, and a look back at the week.

There's a famous kind of photo: the whole Earth from far away, small and round, with everyone anyone has ever known somewhere inside that one shape. The Brahmanda Purana has an older picture like it. An egg, golden, floating on the waters, and holding everything that will ever be: the sky, the earth, the gods, the mountains, the people, the grass. The Purana takes its name from that egg.
screen: `THE WHOLE EARTH IN ONE PHOTO.` → `A GOLDEN EGG ON THE WATERS.` → `EVERYTHING INSIDE.`

segments.voice: The name means Brahma's egg: the whole universe pictured as one shell with everything inside. In the creation story it points to, the egg forms on the waters, Brahma is born inside it, and from it the worlds are laid out, layer by layer: lands and seas, mountains, the skies above. An egg says a few things at once. The universe is one thing; gods and grass share the same shell. It's alive, something that grows from within. And it's held. Now look back at this week from inside that shell. Rice pressed into a body for the road. A hard river, and gifts to cross it. A map, a mirror and a rite, all in one room of mourners. A baby with six star mothers. Fords, more and more of them. A merchant's promise, finally kept. Different books, different gods, different crossings, and every grieving family, pilgrim and merchant in them inside the same egg.
screen: `BRAHMA'S EGG ON THE WATERS.` · `ONE SHELL, ALIVE, HELD.` · `A WEEK INSIDE THE EGG.` · then, large: `GODS TO GRASS, ONE SHELL.`

segments.voice: Hold something round in your hand, an orange, a cup, a smooth stone, and look at it closely for a few breaths. Then let your attention widen: the room, the street, the city, the sky, until it all feels held in one round shape, with you inside it alongside everyone else.
The Brahmanda. The Purana named for Brahma's egg, the whole universe pictured inside one shell.
Your line: the Brahmanda. Everything, gods to grass, inside one shell. A week closes here.

howItsDone: Hindu creation accounts in several Puranas picture the universe as the brahmanda, Brahma's egg; the image appears in temple art and in the way some teachers speak of the cosmos as one living whole.

fork.setup: at dinner a cousin says people from other countries have 'nothing to do with us.' what does the Brahmanda's picture put in front of him?
options: the egg holds only the gods; people aren't in the picture.
everything sits inside one shell, gods to grass, him included.
the egg is about the sky, not about people at all.
fork.reveal: the Brahmanda pictures the whole universe as one shell: gods, mountains, people and grass, all inside the same egg.
